faqs.question: What does the Panel Reactive Antibody (PRA) Screening measure?
faqs.answer: This test measures the presence of class I and class II antibodies in your blood.

faqs.question: Why is PRA Screening done?
faqs.answer: • To evaluate the compatibility between an organ donor and recipient prior to transplantation • To assess the level of sensitisation and reduce the risk of organ rejection due to pre-existing antibodies present in the recipient's blood

faqs.question: When is PRA Screening recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: Your doctor may recommend this test if • you are a candidate for organ transplantation or have previously received a transplant, or • you have been exposed to blood transfusions, pregnancies, or previous transplants.

faqs.question: What if the results of PRA Screening are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Increased levels of class I and/or class II antibodies suggest a higher risk of organ rejection due to pre-existing antibodies.

faqs.question: What to expect during PRA Screening?
faqs.answer: During this test, a blood sample will be collected from you. The sample will be sent to the laboratory for analysis.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before PRA Screening?
faqs.answer: • Inform your doctor about any medications or supplements you are currently taking. Also, tell them if you have any specific requirements. • Follow your doctor's instructions and inform them about any recent blood transfusions, pregnancies, or previous transplants.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with PRA Screening?
faqs.answer: • Human Leucocyte Antigen (HLA) typing: This test determines the specific genetic markers present on your cells, aiding in transplant matching. • Crossmatch test: This test assesses the compatibility between your antibodies and the potential donor's cells. • Transplant workup tests: These tests evaluate your overall health, including kidney and liver function, to ensure successful transplantation.

faqs.question: What is the Panel Reactive Antibody (PRA) Screening also known as?
What is organ transplantation?
faqs.answer: Organ transplantation is a surgical procedure that involves replacing a diseased or failing organ with a healthy one from a donor. It is primarily performed to treat conditions such as kidney, liver, heart, or lung failure. Transplantation offers improved quality of life and increased survival rates for eligible patients.
